nodes.title: Policies and Statements related to climate change
nodes.heading: 1.5 Policies and Statements related to climate change
nodes.start_phrase: With the aim of carrying out an efficient management of the IRO's arising from climate change, the CaixaBank Group has established a global framework for action comprising a number of policies, principles and statements that reflect its commitment to climate change and set out guidelines to help mitigate and adapt to climate change.
nodes.summary:
- Describes CaixaBank Group’s global framework to manage climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs), focused on mitigation and adaptation.
- Identifies two core components of this framework: the Statement on Climate Change and the Corporate Sustainability/ESG Risk Management Policy.
- The Statement on Climate Change sets commitments aligned with the Paris Agreement and outlines proactive lines of action for managing climate issues both directly (own operations) and indirectly (customers, suppliers).
- The Corporate Sustainability/ESG Risk Management Policy sets exclusions, restrictions, and criteria for customer onboarding and financing decisions based on environmental and climate factors.
- References broader governance context in the “Framework of policies, principles and statements in the field of sustainability” and points to further detail in the “Sustainability/ESG risk management” section.

nodes.title: Statement on climate change
nodes.heading: 1.5.1 Statement on climate change
nodes.start_phrase: The Statement on climate change presents CaixaBank's commitment to climate change in relation to the Paris Agreement.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines CaixaBank Group’s global framework for managing climate-related impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs), aimed at efficient mitigation and adaptation to climate change.
- Identifies two core components of this framework: the Statement on Climate Change and the Corporate Sustainability/ESG Risk Management Policy.
- The Statement on Climate Change affirms alignment with the Paris Agreement and commits to a proactive, socially inclusive approach, setting lines of action for both direct operations and the broader value chain (customers, suppliers, etc.).
- The Corporate Sustainability/ESG Risk Management Policy defines exclusions, restrictions, and criteria related to environmental and climate factors for customer onboarding and financing decisions, with further details provided in the Sustainability/ESG risk management section.

nodes.title: Corporate policy on sustainability/ESG risk management
nodes.heading: 1.5.2 Corporate policy on sustainability/ESG risk management
nodes.start_phrase: The Corporate policy on sustainability/ESG risk management includes exclusions, restrictions and criteria that the Group has defined in relation to environmental and climate factors for admitting customers and financing operations.
nodes.summary:
- Describes CaixaBank Group’s global framework for managing climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, setting guidelines to mitigate and adapt to climate change.
- Positions climate policies within the broader sustainability framework, highlighting two core instruments: the Statement on Climate Change and the Corporate Sustainability/ESG Risk Management Policy.
- Explains the Statement on Climate Change as a commitment aligned with the Paris Agreement, outlining proactive, socially inclusive actions for managing climate issues both directly and through stakeholders (customers, suppliers, etc.).
- Outlines the Corporate Sustainability/ESG Risk Management Policy, which defines exclusions, restrictions, and criteria related to environmental and climate factors for customer admission and financing decisions, with further detail referenced in the Sustainability/ESG risk management section.

nodes.title: Climate strategy
nodes.heading: 1.6 Climate strategy
nodes.start_phrase: Below is presented the CaixaBank Group's climate strategy.
nodes.summary:
- The CaixaBank Group positions climate strategy as a core element of its overall sustainability priority, supported by a framework to identify, assess, and measure climate-related risks and opportunities.
- Its approach is embedded in the 2022-2024 Sustainable Banking Plan and the new 2025-2027 Sustainability Plan, aiming to drive the sustainable transition of companies and society.
- Strategic objectives include contributing to a carbon-neutral economy through sustainable financing and investment, proactive climate risk management, and reducing the environmental impact of its own operations.
- A Climate Transition Plan is being developed for completion within 2025-2027; its pillars are sectoral decarbonisation targets and transition plans, a robust governance model, and guiding policies to ensure coherent implementation.
- Execution is structured around two lines of action; the document details the first: developing products and services that facilitate customers’ transition.
- Sustainable finance mobilisation targets: €64 billion for 2022-2024 and €100 billion for 2025-2027.
- Key levers include financing renewable energy, clean mobility, industrial decarbonisation, and energy-efficient buildings; issuing sustainable bonds since 2020; and promoting responsible investment through the Group’s asset and pension plan managers (sustainable intermediation).
- Long-term ambition: a net-zero loan portfolio by 2050 for both businesses and households, alongside direct support to clients and issuers in their decarbonisation efforts.
- The transition is recognized as both a risk and an opportunity, with solutions tailored to meet customer and stakeholder expectations.

nodes.title: 1. Development of products and services to facilitate the transition for customers
nodes.heading: 1.6.1 1. Development of products and services to facilitate the transition for customers
nodes.start_phrase: The transition process towards a more sustainable economy is a source of risk for companies, but it also involves financial opportunities.
nodes.summary:
- Strategic goal: advance toward a more sustainable economy through two lines of action, with the excerpt detailing the first—developing products and services to facilitate customers’ transition.
- Sustainable finance mobilisation targets: €64,000 million during 2022–2024 and €100,000 million targeted for 2025–2027.
- Rationale: the transition poses risks and opportunities; the bank aims to meet customer and stakeholder needs with viable solutions.
- Key actions:
  - Financing sustainable projects in renewable energy, clean mobility, industrial decarbonisation, and energy-efficient housing.
  - Issuing green/sustainable bonds since 2020 to channel funds to these projects.
  - Promoting responsible investment via the asset manager and pension plan manager (sustainable intermediation).
- Focus areas highlighted: renewable energy, clean mobility, efficient buildings, industrial decarbonisation, and sustainable intermediation.
- Decarbonisation commitment: target of a net-zero loan portfolio by 2050 for businesses and households, with support for corporate customers and issuers.
- Reference to additional objectives detailed in the “Sustainable Finance” section.

nodes.title: Target 01. Mobilisation of sustainable financing
nodes.heading: 1.6.1.1 Target 01. Mobilisation of sustainable financing
nodes.start_phrase: As previously mentioned, an opportunity related to financing the customers' transition has been identified, for which CaixaBank has set itself a series of objectives for the mobilisation of sustainable finance.
nodes.summary:
- The document outlines a strategy to advance a more sustainable economy through two lines of action: developing products and services to facilitate customers’ transition, and driving decarbonisation in society and business.
- It sets sustainable finance mobilisation targets of €64,000 million for 2022–2024 and €100,000 million for 2025–2027.
- It frames the transition as both a risk and an opportunity, committing to viable solutions that meet customer and stakeholder expectations.
- Key activities include:
  - Financing sustainable projects in renewable energy, clean mobility, efficient/energy‑efficient buildings, and industrial decarbonisation.
  - Issuing sustainable bonds since 2020 to channel funds to these projects.
  - Promoting responsible investment via the asset manager and pension plan manager (sustainable intermediation).
- Investment priorities are listed as renewable energy, clean mobility, efficient buildings, industrial decarbonisation, and sustainable intermediation.
- Decarbonisation commitments include achieving a net‑zero loan portfolio by 2050 for businesses and households, and providing support to businesses (customers and emitters) in their transition.
- Additional objectives related to sustainable finance are referenced in the “Sustainable Finance” section; this excerpt is from the Management Report 2024.

nodes.title: Objective 02. Achieve zero net emissions by 2050 ( Net Zero )
nodes.heading: 1.6.2 Objective 02. Achieve zero net emissions by 2050 ( Net Zero )
nodes.start_phrase: CaixaBank's ambition is to achieve zero net emission by 2050 and promote the company's decarbonisation arrive at the neutrality in issuances of carbon for 2050 and promote society's decarbonisation.
nodes.summary:
- Objective: Achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 and drive decarbonisation across CaixaBank and society.
- Strategy built on three lines of action:
  1) Align investment and lending portfolios with the Paris Agreement to limit warming to 1.5°C, setting 2030 interim decarbonisation targets in key sectors in line with NZBA and NZAOA.
  2) Reduce the bank’s direct operational footprint through eight pillars defined in the 2022–2024 Environmental Management Plan.
  3) Support clients’ transition with tailored solutions based on their decarbonisation maturity.
- Additional commitment: Evaluate introducing an internal carbon pricing system within the 2025–2027 Sustainability Plan.

nodes.title: Alignment of the investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement
nodes.heading: 1.6.3 Alignment of the investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement
nodes.start_phrase: In order to meet the objective of carbon neutral emissions by 2050, CaixaBank has focused on the decarbonisation of the Group's investment and credit portfolio, emphasising on the more carbon intensive1 sectors through its commitment to the NZBA and NZAOA.
nodes.summary:
- Objective: Align CaixaBank’s investment and credit portfolios with the Paris Agreement to limit warming to 1.5°C and achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, prioritizing carbon‑intensive sectors.
- Commitments: Founding member of the NZBA (Apr 2021, UNEP FI-led); VidaCaixa joined the NZAOA in 2022. NZBA is the banking benchmark; the Bank is working to reconcile NZBA with SBTi without duplicating efforts.
- Scope and approach: Includes financed emissions from clients; sets science-based interim and 2030 targets per UNEP FI guidelines; applies to CaixaBank, S.A. and Banco BPI. No commercial activities identified as incompatible with a climate‑neutral transition.
- Published sector targets:
  - 2022: Electricity generation; Oil & Gas.
  - 2023: Thermal coal; Iron & steel; Automotive.
  - 2024: Real estate (residential and commercial); Maritime; Aviation; Agriculture & livestock. Aluminium and cement deemed non‑material, with portfolio monitoring in place.
- Coverage: Targets now set for all NZBA‑prioritized carbon‑intensive sectors, covering over 43.8% of total corporate and project finance exposure.
- Client transition: Commitment to publish interim targets for most intensive sectors and to support clients with sector‑specific transition plans and targets.
- Assurance and methodology: Targets not yet independently reviewed; developed using best market practices, stakeholder input, and aligned with UNEP FI target‑setting guidance.
- Regulatory note: CaixaBank is not excluded from EU Paris‑aligned benchmarks due to its business nature; will disclose, by 28 March 2025, exposures to companies excluded from those indices per EU Regulation 2020/1818 (prudential report, section 8.4.1, template 1).

nodes.title: NZBA decarbonisation targets
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.1 NZBA decarbonisation targets
nodes.start_phrase: Within the framework of the NZBA, CaixaBank published its first decarbonisation targets3 for 2030 for the electricity generation and oil and gas sectors in October 2022.
nodes.summary:
- Objective: Align CaixaBank’s investment and credit portfolio with the Paris Agreement to reach net-zero by 2050, prioritizing carbon‑intensive sectors through NZBA and NZAOA commitments.
- Alliances and governance: Founding member of NZBA (2021); VidaCaixa joined NZAOA (2022). NZBA is used to set science‑based targets; CaixaBank is working within UNEP FI to reconcile NZBA with SBTi and avoid duplications.
- Scope of commitment: Includes financed emissions from clients (credit portfolio). Interim targets set for priority, high‑emitting sectors per UNEP FI guidance, covering CaixaBank, S.A. and Banco BPI; prioritized sectors represent over 43.8% of total corporate and project finance exposure.
- Methodology and controls: Financed emissions calculated under PCAF’s Global GHG Accounting Standard and externally audited. Target scopes tailored by sector materiality across Scopes 1–3, value‑chain stages, and relevant metrics (absolute, economic, physical). Subject to the Group’s three lines of defence. Pathways generally aligned to 1.5°C scenarios.
- Target‑setting progress: 
  - 2022: First 2030 targets for electricity generation and oil & gas.
  - 2023: Added thermal coal, iron & steel, and automotive.
  - 2024: Added commercial and residential real estate, maritime, aviation, and agriculture & livestock; aluminium and cement deemed non‑material (monitoring only).
- Baselines and ambition: Baseline years chosen for data availability and representativeness (e.g., oil & gas 2020, acknowledging COVID-19 effects makes ambition stronger). CaixaBank will maintain reduction ambition even if baselines or methodologies evolve.
- 2030 sector targets (high level):
  - Power generation: −30% physical intensity (to 95 kg CO2e/MWh).
  - Oil & gas (fossil fuel combustion/financed emissions): −23% absolute emissions.
  - Automotive: −33% Scope 3 intensity (gCO2/vkm).
  - Iron & steel: −10% to −20% Scope 1+2 intensity (kg CO2e/t).
  - Thermal coal: 100% exit from exposure.
  - Commercial real estate: −41% intensity (CRREM 1.5°C Iberia).
  - Residential real estate: −19% intensity (CRREM 1.5°C Spain/Portugal).
  - Maritime: reduce alignment delta to 0% (IMO method).
  - Aviation: −30% intensity (gCO2e/RPK, MPPU 1.5°).
  - Agriculture & livestock: qualitative target focused on improving data and client/sector profiling (SBTi FLAG).
- Notes and disclosures: Commercial real estate and maritime targets are noted elsewhere as not aligned with a 1.5°C pathway. No activities incompatible with a climate‑neutral transition identified. CaixaBank is not excluded from EU‑Paris benchmarks due to its business nature but will disclose exposures to companies excluded from those indices in its March 2025 prudential report. Targets are based on best practices and stakeholder input but are not independently assured.

nodes.title: NZAOA decarbonisation targets
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.2 NZAOA decarbonisation targets
nodes.start_phrase: As part of the NZAOA initiative, VidaCaixa has set intermediate decarbonisation targets (to 2030) for the CaixaBank Group's insurance business, focusing on three areas:
nodes.summary:
- VidaCaixa, under the NZAOA initiative, sets 2030 interim decarbonisation targets for CaixaBank Group’s insurance business across three fronts: portfolio emissions reduction, climate-focused corporate dialogues, and transition finance.
- Portfolio emissions target: cut the scopes 1 and 2 carbon footprint intensity of corporate investments by at least 50% by 2030 versus a 2019 baseline of 177 tCO2 per million euros invested; establish rolling five-year targets after 2030 to reach net zero by 2050 at the latest.
- Target-setting is aligned with the NZAOA protocol and a 1.5°C IPCC “no or limited overshoot” pathway; the 2020–2030 reduction threshold of 40–60% is set at the median 50%.
- Offsetting is not allowed in setting targets for scope 3.15 under the current NZAOA framework; potential long-term use may be considered only after minimizing the carbon footprint.
- Climate stewardship: engage at least 20 carbon‑intensive companies (or those responsible for 65% of portfolio emissions) to improve their climate targets, leveraging channels such as Climate Action 100+ and contributing to alliance-led decarbonisation reports.
- Transition finance: actively support the energy transition via climate-positive instruments, including green bonds (e.g., for energy efficiency) and thematic climate funds.
- Governance: NZBA decarbonisation targets are approved by the Board; cross-functional groups meet weekly to track operations affecting NZBA metrics; monthly updates go to the Sustainability and Global Risk Committees; annual reporting to the Management Committee, the Appointments and Sustainability Committee, and the Risks Committee.
- Monitoring and integration: VidaCaixa regularly tracks exposure to carbon‑intensive sectors and portfolio carbon footprint, incorporates climate metrics and ESG assessments into investment decisions, and reports significant progress in reducing the insurance investment portfolio’s carbon footprint.

nodes.title: Governance of decarbonisation targets
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.3 Governance of decarbonisation targets
nodes.start_phrase: The set NZBA decarbonisation targets have been approved by the Board of Directors.
nodes.summary:
- VidaCaixa, under the NZAOA initiative, sets 2030 interim decarbonisation targets for CaixaBank Group’s insurance business across three pillars: portfolio emissions cuts, climate-focused corporate engagement, and transition financing.
- Portfolio emissions target: reduce scopes 1 and 2 carbon footprint of corporate investments by at least 50% by 2030 versus a 2019 baseline of 177 tCO2 per million euros invested; reset targets every five years to reach net zero by 2050 at the latest.
- Targets align with NZAOA protocol and science-based thresholds (40–60% reduction for 2020–2030; VidaCaixa adopts the 50% midpoint) and use the IPCC 1.5°C “no/limited overshoot” scenario.
- Offsetting is not permitted for setting NZAOA decarbonisation targets (including scope 3.15); the role of offsets may be reconsidered long term once residual emissions are minimized.
- Climate dialogues: engage with at least 20 carbon‑intensive companies or those responsible for 65% of portfolio emissions; leverage initiatives like Climate Action 100+ and contribute to alliance-led decarbonisation reports.
- Transition financing: proactively fund climate‑positive solutions (e.g., green bonds for energy efficiency, thematic climate funds).
- Governance: decarbonisation targets (referred to as NZBA in the governance section) approved by the Board; cross‑functional groups meet weekly to review operations affecting metrics; monthly reporting to the Sustainability and Global Risk Committees; annual updates to the Management, Appointments & Sustainability, and Risks Committees.
- Ongoing monitoring of exposure to carbon‑intensive sectors and portfolio carbon footprint, integrating climate metrics and ESG assessments into investment decisions, leading to significant reductions in the insurance investment portfolio’s carbon footprint.

nodes.title: Transition plans and alignment
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4 Transition plans and alignment
nodes.start_phrase: Since setting the first NZBA targets, CaixaBank has been actively managing its sectoral portfolios to ensure that the transition to the targets set for each sector are properly met.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of CaixaBank’s approach to aligning sectoral portfolios with NZBA decarbonisation targets, emphasizing active management since initial target setting.
- Acknowledgment that portfolio decarbonisation may be non-linear due to the bank’s focus on supporting customers through their transition.
- Key action pillars to manage alignment metrics:
  - Measurement and monitoring: emission intensity limits for new business; CO2 and climate impact assessment for all new transactions; updated metrics for recent positions; analysis of change drivers; systematic review of clients’ climate transition plans.
  - Control and admission policies: sustainability risk “red lines” integrated into risk admission; review and penalization measures for new operations not aligned.
  - Client dialogue and engagement: assessment and classification of key clients’ alignment to sustainability indicators; strategies to improve performance; provision of products and services to facilitate transition.
- Indication that detailed sectoral alignment plans and customer transition progress are provided for all sectors with targets.
- Recognition that decarbonisation outcomes depend on external factors such as government policy, regulation, consumer behavior, scientific advances, and new technologies.

nodes.title: Electricity sector
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.1 Electricity sector
nodes.start_phrase: The electricity's baseline (136 kg CO2e/MWh) is much lower than that of most entities that have disclosed targets for this sector to date, and it is even below the IEA's target metric by 2030.
nodes.summary:
- Focus and scope: The analysis targets the electricity generation segment—where decarbonisation has the greatest sector impact—and includes integrated utilities. Scope 1 emissions are covered; Scope 2 is excluded due to minimal materiality, and Scope 3 is excluded because it is hard to influence from the generation side and addressed in other sector targets.
- Metric and reference pathway: Uses a physical intensity metric (kg CO2e/MWh) to allow comparability across customer sizes and support growth in efficient groups. The reference pathway is the IEA Net Zero 2050 scenario. Risk considered is exposure (limit granted).
- Baseline and rationale: 2020 baseline intensity is 136 kg CO2e/MWh, significantly lower than most peers and below the IEA’s 2030 target level. This reflects CaixaBank’s long-standing financing of renewables, evidenced by green bond issuances from 2020 to 2024.
- 2030 target: A 30% reduction in intensity by 2030, reaching 95 kg CO2e/MWh.
- Progress and trajectory: The metric’s evolution is non-linear but trending favorably, with 78% of the 2030 target already achieved. The low starting point limits further reduction margin, and progress has been made despite a challenging geopolitical energy context.
- Visualization highlights: The trajectory shows CaixaBank’s intensity below the IEA NZE 2030 benchmark (around 156 kg CO2e/MWh) from the baseline onward, and tracking toward the 95 kg CO2e/MWh 2030 objective.
- Key design decisions (summary): 
  1) Value chain focus on generation (including integrated companies). 
  2) Emissions scope limited to Scope 1. 
  3) Emissions metric is physical intensity (kg CO2e/MWh). 
  4) Decarbonisation pathway aligned to IEA Net Zero 2050. 
  5) Risk lens based on exposure (limit granted).

nodes.title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.1.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.start_phrase: A reduction target for the 2030 intensity metric of 30% has been set, with the following characteristics:
nodes.summary:
- Focus and scope: The alignment metric targets the electricity sector, concentrating on the generation segment where decarbonisation has the greatest impact, and includes integrated companies across the value chain. Only Scope 1 emissions are included; Scope 2 is immaterial and Scope 3 is difficult to influence from generation and is covered by other sector targets.
- Metric and reference pathway: Uses a physical emissions intensity metric (kg CO2e/MWh) to enable comparability across different-sized clients and support growth in more efficient groups. The reference pathway is the IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 (NZE 2050) scenario. Risk considered is exposure (limit granted).
- Baseline performance: 2020 baseline intensity is 136 kg CO2e/MWh, which is lower than most peer disclosures and even below the IEA’s 2030 target metric (~156 kg CO2e/MWh). This reflects CaixaBank’s long-standing financing of renewables, including green bond issuances from 2020 to 2024.
- 2030 target: A 30% reduction from the 2020 baseline, targeting 95 kg CO2e/MWh by 2030, exceeding the IEA’s implied 2030 reduction (-23%).
- Progress and trajectory: The evolution of the metric is favorable though not linear; approximately 78% of the 2030 reduction has already been achieved, with recent intensity around 105 kg CO2e/MWh. The trajectory remains ambitious given the already low baseline relative to the sector’s IEA NZE 2050 benchmark.
- Constraints and context: Further decarbonisation is challenging due to the low starting point and a complex geopolitical environment for the energy sector, yet CaixaBank maintains its ambition to continue leading renewable energy financing.

nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.1.2 Evolution of the metric

nodes.title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.1.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.start_phrase: For CaixaBank, the ultimate goal of the decarbonisation strategy for its portfolio in the electricity sector is to guide its customers in their transition to a less emission-intensive generation mix, provided that they are committed to sustainability.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: CaixaBank’s sector transition plan centers on decarbonizing its electricity and oil & gas (O&G) portfolios by guiding customers toward lower-emission models and aligning financing with net‑zero pathways.
- Electricity sector approach:
  - Goal: Reduce portfolio emissions intensity by helping customers shift to less emission‑intensive generation mixes.
  - Levers: Increase financing of renewables and engage strategically with clients to provide solutions that meet or accelerate their decarbonization plans.
  - Portfolio management: Consider rebalancing toward lower‑emission clients and derisking or exiting counterparties not committed to a low‑carbon transition.
- Oil & gas sector alignment:
  - Target metric: Absolute emissions metric, reflecting industry expectations; decarbonization driven by energy efficiency and fuel substitution (demand effects).
  - Recent context: 2022 saw a temporary rise in O&G exposure due to energy security/geopolitical factors to ensure short/medium‑term supply, causing potential metric volatility but not altering medium/long‑term decarbonization commitments.
  - Ambition: A 23% reduction target versus 2020 is effectively more ambitious given the atypical baseline conditions.
- Boundary and methodology:
  - Value chain: Upstream (exploration/extraction), downstream (refining, distribution, marketing), and integrated companies; this captures most sector emissions.
  - Emissions scope: Scopes 1, 2, and 3, with scope 3 recognized as highly material for O&G.
  - Standards alignment: Approach aligned with the NZBA Guide, stakeholder expectations, and peer practices; reference pathway is the IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 (NZE2050).
  - Measurement basis: Absolute emissions calculated using risk drawn down (not risk granted) to avoid over‑attribution, consistent with PCAF and enabling peer comparability.
  - Key design decisions summarized: value chain coverage, full scope (1–3) accounting, absolute emissions metric based on risk drawn down, IEA NZE2050 pathway selection, and risk considered as drawn down.

nodes.title: Oil and gas sector
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.2 Oil and gas sector
nodes.start_phrase: The decarbonisation target is based on an absolute emissions metric, in line with industry expectations.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines CaixaBank’s sector transition plan for electricity, aiming to guide committed customers toward a less emission‑intensive generation mix, thereby lowering the bank’s portfolio intensity.
- Identifies key levers: financing renewable energy and active engagement with strategic customers to help meet or accelerate their decarbonisation plans.
- Notes possible portfolio rebalancing toward lower‑emission clients and derisking from counterparties not committed to a low‑carbon transition.
- Defines the oil and gas sector decarbonisation target using an absolute emissions metric, reflecting industry expectations.
- Explains that decarbonisation in oil and gas will come from energy efficiency improvements and demand‑side fuel substitution.
- Acknowledges atypical recent energy‑security dynamics; 2022 saw a temporary increase in O&G exposure to ensure supply, creating potential metric volatility but not altering medium/long‑term decarbonisation commitments.
- States the 23% alignment objective (from a 2020 baseline) is effectively more ambitious given these extraordinary conditions.
- Sets the oil and gas alignment perimeter and methodology: covers upstream, downstream, and integrated companies; includes Scopes 1, 2, and 3 (with Scope 3 highly material); metric based on risk drawn down (per PCAF) to avoid over‑attribution; aligned with NZBA guidance and peer practices; uses IEA Net Zero 2050 (NZE2050) as the reference pathway.
- Summarises key design decisions: value chain coverage, full scope emissions, absolute emissions metric based on risk drawn down, NZE2050 pathway, and risk considered as risk drawn down.

nodes.title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.3.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.start_phrase: A reduction target for the 2030 intensity metric of 33% has been set, with the following characteristics:
nodes.summary:
- CaixaBank sets a 2030 target to cut the automotive portfolio’s emissions intensity by 33% from a 2022 baseline.
- Baseline and target: 154.1 gCO2/vkm in 2022; target of 103.1 gCO2/vkm by 2030.
- Progress: the intensity metric has already declined (e.g., ~146 gCO2/vkm in 2023, about -6% vs 2022), deemed on track toward the 2030 goal; CaixaBank will continue efforts through 2030.
- Sector transition plan with customers focuses on accelerating a more energy- and emission-efficient vehicle fleet, primarily via increased production of electric vehicles; success depends on advances in public policy, infrastructure rollout, and technological innovation.
- Value chain focus: light vehicle OEMs (cars and vans), where European decarbonisation efforts are concentrated.
- Emissions scope: Scope 3 Category 11 (use-phase, tank-to-wheel), identified as the most material across the sector’s value chain.
- Metric: physical emissions intensity measured as gCO2 per vehicle-kilometre over a vehicle’s lifetime.
- Reference pathway: aligned to the IEA Net Zero Emissions 2050 (NZE2050) pathway; CaixaBank tracks its trajectory against this path.
- Risk lens: considers portfolio exposure (limit granted) in assessing and managing decarbonisation progress.

nodes.title: Evolution of the metric
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.3.2 Evolution of the metric
nodes.start_phrase: The reduction observed in the intensity metric in the automotive sector is in line with meeting the target set by 2030.
nodes.summary:
- CaixaBank sets a 2030 target to cut the automotive portfolio’s emissions intensity by 33%, from a 2022 baseline of 154.1 gCO2/vkm to 103.1 gCO2/vkm, aligned with the IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 pathway.
- Progress to date indicates a roughly 6% reduction since 2022 (e.g., about 154 to 146 gCO2/vkm), and the trajectory is considered on track toward the 2030 ambition.
- Sector transition plan focuses on client engagement to accelerate a more energy- and emissions-efficient vehicle fleet, with higher electric vehicle (EV) production as the main lever.
- Enablers for EV uptake include supportive public policies, expanded charging and related infrastructure, and continued technological innovation.
- Scope and boundaries: concentrates on light vehicle OEMs (cars and vans), targeting Scope 3 Category 11 (use-phase, tank-to-wheel) emissions, identified as the most material in the value chain.
- Metric: a physical intensity measure (gCO2/vkm) representing lifetime emissions efficiency per kilometer for manufactured vehicles.
- Key design decisions summarized: value chain focus, emissions scope, emissions metric, pathway selection (IEA NZE2050), and risk consideration (exposure/limit granted).
- A plotted pathway shows the bank’s metric trending toward the IEA-aligned objective and the 2030 target level.

nodes.title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.3.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.start_phrase: The priority for the sector's decarbonisation is related to producing a fleet of vehicles that is more energy and emission efficient, where the higher production of electric vehicles is the main vector in reaching this target.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: CaixaBank’s 2030 decarbonisation targets and methodologies for the automotive and iron & steel sectors, as presented in the 2024 Management Report, including scope boundaries, intensity metrics, reference pathways, risk lens, and customer engagement actions.

- Automotive (light vehicle OEMs):
  - Target: 33% reduction in use-phase emissions intensity by 2030, from 154.1 gCO2/vkm (2022 baseline) to 103.1 gCO2/vkm.
  - Scope and metric: Scope 3 Category 11 (tank-to-wheel) lifetime emissions per vehicle-kilometre (gCO2/vkm); aligned with IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 (NZE2050).
  - Progress: Observed decline in the intensity metric (noted ~−6% early trend) is consistent with reaching the 2030 target.
  - Strategy and levers: Customer engagement; financing of projects to produce more efficient and electric vehicles; portfolio rebalancing toward less carbon‑intensive clients. Acknowledges dependencies on supportive public policy, charging infrastructure rollout, and technological innovation. Interim measures include improving ICE efficiency and using lower‑emission renewable/synthetic fuels until full fleet electrification.

- Iron & steel:
  - Target: Range of 10%–20% reduction in emissions intensity by 2030, from 1,230 kgCO2e/t steel (2022 baseline) to 1,107–984 kgCO2e/t steel.
  - Rationale for range: Low but concentrated exposure to a few counterparties, hard‑to‑abate technological constraints, and uncertainty in methodologies and scenarios.
  - Scope and metric: Scopes 1 and 2 emissions intensity per tonne of steel produced (kgCO2e/t); aligned with IEA NZE2050 and Sustainable Steel Principles. Focus on smelting/manufacturing where emissions are most material; upstream/downstream use-phase emissions are less material for this metric.

- Cross-cutting design choices:
  - Value chain boundaries defined per sector (OEMs for autos; smelters/integrated groups for steel).
  - Emissions scopes selected for materiality (Scope 3 Cat. 11 for autos; Scopes 1–2 for steel).
  - Physical intensity metrics used for alignment and tracking.
  - Reference pathway: IEA NZE2050.
  - Risk lens: exposure measured via limits granted to counterparties.

nodes.title: Iron and steel sector
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.4 Iron and steel sector
nodes.start_phrase: In view of the relatively low exposure in the iron and steel sector and its high concentration in a few counterparties, the current technological limitations of a "hard to abate" sector and the uncertainty of methodological and scenario changes, it was decided to set a target in the form of a range for this sector.
nodes.summary:
- Transitional decarbonisation of road transport: Until full vehicle electrification is achieved, CaixaBank aims to cut emissions by supporting more efficient internal combustion technologies, promoting renewable/synthetic low‑carbon fuels, engaging customers, financing projects that increase production of efficient or electric vehicles, and rebalancing lending toward less carbon‑intensive clients.

- Iron and steel sector strategy and targets:
  - Rationale for target design: Given low portfolio exposure concentrated in few counterparties, the sector’s hard‑to‑abate nature, and methodological/scenario uncertainty, CaixaBank set a 2030 target as a range rather than a single point.
  - Methodology: Aligned with market best practice and the Sustainable Steel Principles; uses emissions intensity (Scope 1 and 2) per tonne of steel produced, focusing on production where emissions are most material; use‑phase and upstream supply chain emissions are comparatively less material.
  - Target: Reduce intensity by 10%–20% by 2030 from a 2022 baseline of 1,230 kgCO2e/t steel, reaching 1,107–984 kgCO2e/t steel by 2030.
  - Scope and value chain: Covers iron and steel manufacturing, with emphasis on smelters and integrated groups (smelting plus transformation), as smelting concentrates most emissions.
  - Reference pathway: International Energy Agency Net Zero Emissions by 2050 (NZE2050).
  - Key design decisions: 
    - Value chain focus on foundry/integrated operations within steel manufacturing.
    - Emissions scope limited to Scopes 1 and 2 (material in production).
    - Metric is physical emissions intensity (kgCO2e per tonne of steel).
    - Pathway selection aligned to IEA NZE2050.
    - Risk lens considers portfolio exposure (limits granted).

nodes.title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.4.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.start_phrase: A reduction target for the 2030 intensity metric within a range of 10%-20% has been set, with the following characteristics:
nodes.summary:
- Transportation sector decarbonisation: Until full vehicle electrification is achieved, emissions reduction can progress via more efficient internal combustion technologies and the use of renewable or synthetic fuels. CaixaBank supports this through customer engagement, financing projects for more efficient and electric vehicles, and rebalancing its portfolio toward less carbon-intensive clients.

- Iron and steel sector strategy and targets:
  - Context: Low portfolio exposure concentrated in few counterparties; sector is hard to abate; methodological and scenario uncertainty. Therefore, a target range is used.
  - Methodology: Aligned with market best practice and the Sustainable Steel Principles; uses an emissions intensity metric covering Scope 1 and 2 per tonne of steel produced. Emissions from product use and upstream supply are less material.
  - 2030 target: Reduce emissions intensity by 10%–20% from a 2022 baseline of 1,230 kgCO2e/t steel to 1,107–984 kgCO2e/t steel by 2030.
  - Scope and boundary: Iron and steel manufacturing segment, including smelters and integrated groups (smelting is the most emission-intensive stage); Scopes 1 and 2 are included.
  - Metric: Physical emissions intensity (kgCO2e per tonne of steel).
  - Reference pathway: IEA Net Zero Emissions by 2050 (NZE2050).
  - Risk/portfolio considerations: Exposure (limit granted) is a key risk factor in target design and monitoring.

nodes.title: Evolution of the metric
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.4.2 Evolution of the metric
nodes.start_phrase: The reduction observed in the intensity metric in the iron and steel sector is in line with meeting the ambitious target set by 2030.
nodes.summary:
- Document scope: CaixaBank’s Management Report 2024 excerpt on sector alignment metrics, targets, and transition actions for high-emitting sectors (iron & steel and thermal coal).
- Iron & steel sector:
  - The portfolio intensity metric (kgCO2e/t steel) has fallen and is on track for the 2030 target, with a reported trend of around -13% since 2022.
  - CaixaBank will continue efforts to reduce this metric through 2030.
  - Transition plan with customers acknowledges decarbonization complexity and applies prudence in portfolio management.
  - Levers include client engagement and portfolio rebalancing.
  - An intermediate ambition compatible with a 1.5°C pathway targets a 10%–20% reduction, with the lower bound aligned to the IEA Net Zero (NZE) arrival level.
- Coal sector (thermal coal) alignment metric:
  - Design centers on a complete phase-out of exposure to thermal coal by 2030, reflecting the sector’s anticipated disappearance and high emissions profile.
  - CaixaBank will cease financing companies related to thermal coal, targeting zero exposure by 2030, in line with IPCC guidance.
  - 2022 baseline exposure: €2,845m; 2030 arrival level: €0 (–100%).
  - Current exposure mainly involves counterparts with mitigating factors (financing restricted to energy transition purposes or clients with their own pre‑2030 phase-out commitments).
  - Up to 2030, CaixaBank will continue financing activities that support the energy transition and customers executing credible exit strategies from thermal coal.
  - Exposure definition: companies whose economic group derives more than 5% of revenues from thermal coal.

nodes.title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.4.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.start_phrase: CaixaBank acknowledges the difficulty implicit in the decarbonisation of this sector, which leads it to consider a certain level of prudence in terms of the management margin for decarbonising the portfolio.
nodes.summary:
- Iron and steel sector: CaixaBank reports a decline in its intensity metric, moving toward its 2030 target. The metric fell about 13%, from 1,141 kgCO2e/t steel in 2022 to 984 in 2023, and the bank will continue reducing it through 2030. Its approach includes customer engagement and portfolio rebalancing to pursue an intermediate target compatible with a 1.5 °C pathway, reflecting a 10–20% reduction ambition aligned with IEA Net Zero assumptions at the lower bound. The bank recognizes decarbonization challenges and adopts a prudent management margin while leveraging customer ambition as a key driver.

- Coal sector: CaixaBank sets a full phase-out of thermal coal exposure by 2030, ceasing to finance companies related to thermal coal and reducing exposure to zero. Baseline exposure in 2022 was €2,845m, with a 2030 arrival level of €0 (-100%). Current exposure mainly involves counterparts with mitigating factors: financing limited to energy transition activities or clients that have their own thermal coal phase-out commitments before 2030. Up to 2030, the bank will continue supporting customers’ transition and exit strategies. Exposure is defined as holdings (credit and investment across CaixaBank, S.A. and BPI) in companies whose economic group is more than 5% dependent on thermal coal.

nodes.title: Coal sector
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.5 Coal sector
nodes.start_phrase: Due to thermal coal being one of the highest emitting technologies that can be replaced by clean technologies, the decarbonisation focuses on reducing the entity's entire exposure to thermal coal (phase-out) by 2030: CaixaBank will cease to finance companies related to thermal coal reducing its exposure to zero1.
nodes.summary:
- Focus on decarbonization progress and targets in two high-emitting sectors: iron and steel, and thermal coal.
- Iron and steel:
  - The sector’s emissions intensity metric has fallen, showing a 13% reduction from 2022 to 2023 (from roughly 1,141 to 984 kgCO2e per tonne of steel), trending in line with achieving the 2030 objective.
  - CaixaBank will continue to reduce this metric through 2030.
  - Given the complexity of steel decarbonization, CaixaBank adopts a prudent approach but identifies levers that depend on customer ambition.
  - Through customer engagement and portfolio rebalancing, CaixaBank targets an intermediate pathway aligned with a 1.5°C scenario, setting a 10–20% reduction range that reflects ambition and references IEA Net Zero (NZE) guidance.
- Thermal coal:
  - Alignment metric is exposure-based with a full phase-out by 2030; CaixaBank will cease financing companies linked to thermal coal, reducing exposure to zero, consistent with IPCC guidance and the sector’s anticipated disappearance.
  - 2022 baseline exposure: €2,845 million; 2030 arrival level: €0; ambition: −100%.
  - Current exposure largely involves counterparties with mitigating factors: financing limited to energy transition purposes or clients with their own coal phase-out commitments before 2030.
  - Until 2030, CaixaBank will continue financing activities that support the transition to a carbon-neutral economy and assist clients executing exit strategies from thermal coal.
  - Exposure definition: companies whose economic group derives more than 5% of revenue from thermal coal, covering credit and investments at CaixaBank, S.A. and BPI.

nodes.title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.5.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.start_phrase: A phase out target by 2030 has been set, with the following characteristics:
nodes.summary:
- Reports progress on decarbonization in the iron and steel sector: CaixaBank’s financed emissions intensity fell (from 1,141 to 984 kgCO2e per tonne of steel between 2022 and 2023, a -13% trend), staying on track for its 2030 objective, with continued reductions planned through 2030.
- Outlines a sector transition plan focused on customer engagement and portfolio rebalancing. Acknowledges the complexity of decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors and applies prudence, while pursuing an intermediate target aligned with a 1.5°C pathway. Sets an ambition range of a 10–20% reduction, referencing IEA Net Zero (NZE) guidance.
- Details the coal sector alignment metric: a full thermal coal phase-out by 2030. CaixaBank will cease financing companies related to thermal coal, reducing exposure to zero by 2030, consistent with IPCC guidance and the sector’s anticipated decline.
- Notes current coal exposure largely involves counterparts with mitigating factors (financing limited to energy transition purposes or firms with their own pre‑2030 thermal coal exit commitments).
- Quantifies the coal target: baseline exposure of €2,845m in 2022 to €0 by 2030 (-100%). Defines exposure as holdings in groups with >5% dependence on thermal coal, covering credit and investments of CaixaBank, S.A. and BPI.
- Commits to continue financing the energy transition and supporting clients with credible thermal coal exit strategies up to 2030.

nodes.title: Evolution of the metric
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.5.2 Evolution of the metric
nodes.start_phrase: The evolution of the metric in relation to the baseline is slightly upward, due to matters related to data quality.
nodes.summary:
- The alignment metric shows a slight uptick versus the baseline, attributed to data quality issues, while CaixaBank remains committed to its 2030 phase‑out target.
- Sector transition plan for thermal coal: no new approvals or renewals at maturity for customers linked to thermal coal; remaining positions will be sold to ensure zero exposure by 2030.
- Commercial real estate (CRE) alignment approach:
  - Recognizes sector complexity, limited availability of actual emissions data, and significant geographic variability; continued use of proxies where needed.
  - Sets an ambitious target and prioritizes improving data quality, especially EPC availability and asset‑level emissions information.
  - Achievement is conditional on national and EU energy efficiency and energy mix trajectories (PNIEC current and draft, Fit for 55, etc.).
- CRE metric design:
  - Value chain focus on the “use” phase of properties (where ~85% of GHG emissions occur) and on non‑residential building owners.
  - Emissions scope: Scope 1 (on‑site fuel combustion) and Scope 2 (purchased energy).
  - Metric: physical emissions intensity (kgCO2e/m2) to enable comparability and incentivize more efficient assets.
  - Reference pathway: CRREM 1.5°C REC, prorated by asset type for Spain and Portugal (core geographies).
- Monitoring and reporting:
  - CaixaBank tracks CRE emissions‑intensity trends through 2030, comparing results with and without mitigating factors against the CRREM pathway.

nodes.title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.5.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.start_phrase: As part of the commitment undertaken, the Entity's transition plan for this sector consists in not approving and renewing any positions and/or operations at maturity with customers linked to thermal coal.
nodes.summary:
- The metric’s trend versus baseline is slightly upward due to data quality issues, but CaixaBank reaffirms its 2030 phase-out commitment.
- Sector transition plan for thermal coal: no new approvals or renewals at maturity for customers linked to thermal coal; residual positions to be sold to achieve zero exposure by 2030.
- Commercial real estate (CRE) alignment approach:
  - Complex sector with limited actual emissions data; continued use of proxies and emphasis on improving EPC availability and asset-level emissions information.
  - Geographic variability influences targets; CaixaBank sets an ambitious target despite data constraints.
  - Achievement of targets depends on national/EU energy efficiency and energy mix trajectories (PNIEC, draft PNIEC, Fit for 55).
- Focus of decarbonization: the “use” phase of non-residential properties (responsible for ~85% of GHG emissions), targeting building owners.
- Emissions scope: Scope 1 (on-site fuel combustion) and Scope 2 (purchased energy).
- Metric: physical emissions intensity (kgCO2e/m2), encouraging more efficient assets and enabling comparison across asset sizes.
- Reference pathway: CRREM 1.5°C REC scenario, prorated by non-residential asset types in Spain and Portugal (Iberian Peninsula).
- Monitoring and trajectory: presentation of CaixaBank metrics with and without mitigating factors and their trend versus the CRREM pathway through 2030.
- Key design decisions summarized: value chain focus, scopes covered, chosen intensity metric, and CRREM-based pathway for CRE in the Iberian Peninsula.

nodes.title: Commercial real estate sector
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.6 Commercial real estate sector
nodes.start_phrase: The commercial real estate sector is a complex sector and, to date, the availability of actual emissions data remains limited, which is why the use of proxies in the alignment calculations is still important.
nodes.summary:
- The metric’s evolution versus baseline shows a slight upward trend, attributed to data quality issues, though CaixaBank reaffirms its commitment to meet the 2030 phase-out target.
- Sector transition plan for customers linked to thermal coal: no approvals or renewals at maturity; remaining positions will be sold if needed to achieve zero exposure by 2030.
- Commercial real estate alignment approach:
  - Focus on decarbonising the “use” phase of properties, targeting owners of non-residential assets where ~85% of GHG emissions occur.
  - Emissions scope covered: Scope 1 (on-site fuel combustion) and Scope 2 (purchased energy).
  - Metric: physical emissions intensity (kgCO2e/m2), enabling comparison across asset sizes and encouraging more efficient assets.
  - Reference pathway: CRREM 1.5°C decarbonisation pathway, adapted to the non-residential stock in Spain and Portugal (main geographies).
- Data and methodology:
  - Limited availability of actual emissions data in the sector necessitates proxies; CaixaBank prioritises improving EPC coverage and asset-level emissions information.
  - Targets are sensitive to geographic differences and pathway selections.
- Dependencies and assumptions:
  - Achieving targets depends on meeting energy efficiency and energy mix trajectories in national and EU policies (PNIEC, draft PNIEC, Fit for 55, etc.).
- Reporting/monitoring:
  - Trends are shown for CaixaBank’s metric with and without mitigating factors, benchmarked against the chosen pathway, indicating ongoing alignment management through 2030.

nodes.title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.6.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.start_phrase: A reduction target for the 2030 intensity metric of 41% has been set, with the following characteristics:
nodes.summary:
- Sets a 2030 target to cut commercial real estate portfolio emissions intensity by 41%, from a 2022 baseline of 20.5 kgCO2e/m2 to 12.1 kgCO2e/m2.
- Notes the metric was largely stable from 2022 to 2023 (about 20.5 to 20.1 kgCO2e/m2), reflecting reliance on proxies; prioritizes improving data quality, especially EPC coverage and asset emissions data.
- Outlines a customer-focused transition plan: decarbonize by financing new buildings with higher energy ratings and retrofitting existing stock (better insulation/façades/windows/envelopes, installing solar panels, and upgrading to more efficient HVAC systems). First step is expanding EPC and emissions information across the portfolio.
- For residential real estate, explains the alignment metric accounts for social sensitivity, long loan maturities, and dependence on external levers (regulation and public aid); therefore, the initial target is not aligned with the CRREM pathway.
- Commits to leveraging policy and regulatory changes and shifts in consumer behavior, and to launching specific financing products for energy-efficient home retrofits, contributing to the broader net-zero transition.
- Presents a trajectory showing a modest early reduction (~-2% from 2022 to 2023) toward the 2030 target and comparison with the CRREM 1.5°C pathway.

nodes.title: Evolution of the metric
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.6.2 Evolution of the metric
nodes.start_phrase: The commercial real estate metric remained reasonably stable between 2022 and 2023.
nodes.summary:
- CaixaBank sets a 2030 target to cut commercial real estate emissions intensity by 41%, from 20.5 kgCO2e/m2 in 2022 to 12.1 kgCO2e/m2 by 2030.
- Metric evolution shows stability from 2022 to 2023 (20.5 to 20.1 kgCO2e/m2, about -2%), attributed to reliance on proxies; improving portfolio data quality is a priority.
- Sector transition plan focuses on working with customers to:
  - Increase availability of EPCs and asset-level emissions data.
  - Finance new buildings with higher energy ratings.
  - Support retrofits to existing stock (enhanced insulation, façade/window/envelope restoration, solar panel installation, and energy-efficient HVAC replacement).
- As data improves, financing will prioritize assets with better energy performance and restoration projects that boost efficiency.
- Residential real estate approach: target is not initially aligned with the CRREM 1.5°C pathway due to social sensitivity, long loan maturities, and dependence on external levers (regulation, public incentives).
- CaixaBank plans to leverage policy changes, regulatory developments, and consumer behavior shifts, and is launching specific financing products for energy-efficient home retrofits.
- A chart illustrates the CaixaBank metric trend versus the CRREM 1.5°C path, showing the planned decline to 12.1 kgCO2e/m2 by 2030.

nodes.title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.6.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.start_phrase: The decarbonisation of the commercial real estate can be achieved by adding to the stock new buildings with better EPCs or by improving those of the current stock.
nodes.summary:
- CaixaBank sets a 41% reduction target in carbon intensity (kgCO2e/m2) for its commercial real estate portfolio by 2030, moving from a 2022 baseline of 20.5 to 12.1 by 2030.
- The metric remained largely stable from 2022 to 2023 (around a 2% decrease), reflecting reliance on proxy data; improving data quality—especially EPCs and asset emissions information—is a priority.
- Sector transition plan focuses on working with customers to decarbonize by:
  - Adding new buildings with better energy performance certificates (EPCs).
  - Retrofitting existing stock through improved insulation (façades, windows, envelopes), installing solar panels, and upgrading to more efficient HVAC systems.
  - Using enhanced data to finance both efficient new builds and renovation projects that lift energy performance.
- For residential real estate, the alignment metric is not initially tied to the CRREM pathway due to social sensitivity, long maturities, and dependence on regulatory and public-aid levers.
- CaixaBank will leverage policy changes, environmental regulations, and shifts in consumer behavior, and is launching specific products to finance energy-efficient home retrofits.
- The CRREM 1.5°C pathway is referenced as a benchmark, with CaixaBank’s own trajectory showing a planned decline toward 2030.

nodes.title: Residential real estate sector
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.7 Residential real estate sector
nodes.start_phrase: Given the specific characteristics of the residential real estate segment, its social sensitivity, long maturity periods and dependence on exogenous levers for its transformation (regulatory requirements and public aid to enhance energy efficiency), the target set for the Residential Real Estate Sector is not initially aligned with the CRREM reference path.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: CaixaBank’s 2030 climate target and transition approach for its real estate portfolios (commercial and residential).
- 2030 target (commercial real estate): Reduce financed emissions intensity by 41% from a 2022 baseline of 20.5 kgCO2e/m2 to 12.1 kgCO2e/m2 by 2030.
- Current evolution: Metric remained broadly stable from 2022 to 2023 (around 20.5 to 20.1 kgCO2e/m2), reflecting heavy reliance on proxies; priority is improving portfolio data quality, especially EPC and asset-level emissions information.
- Decarbonisation levers with customers (commercial real estate): 
  - Add new buildings with better energy performance certificates (EPCs).
  - Retrofit existing stock via improved insulation (façades, windows, envelopes), solar PV installation, and upgrading to more efficient HVAC systems.
  - Financing will prioritize both high-efficiency new builds and restoration projects once data coverage improves.
- Residential real estate approach:
  - The initial target is not aligned with the CRREM pathway due to social sensitivity, long loan maturities, and strong dependence on external drivers (regulation, public incentives).
  - CaixaBank will leverage government policies, evolving climate regulations, and consumer behavior shifts, and is launching products to finance energy-efficiency retrofits, contributing to the broader net‑zero transition.
- Reference pathway: CRREM 1.5°C trajectory is cited for context, though residential targets are not initially aligned.

nodes.title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.7.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.start_phrase: A reduction target for the 2030 intensity metric of 19% has been set, with the following characteristics:
nodes.summary:
- Sets a 2030 decarbonization target for CaixaBank’s residential real estate portfolio: a 19% reduction in the physical emissions intensity metric from a 2022 baseline of 23.57 kgCO2e/m2 to 19.03 kgCO2e/m2.
- Notes current performance: the residential real estate intensity has remained largely stable since the baseline year; progress is highly dependent on changes in the energy mix.
- Defines transition actions with customers: decarbonize through refurbishing existing dwellings and constructing new, higher-efficiency buildings; improve availability of Energy Performance Certificates (EPCs) and building emissions data; due to the sector’s social sensitivity, CaixaBank’s direct levers are limited, so it will rely on and support governmental regulations and broader collective initiatives toward net zero.
- Clarifies value chain focus: mortgage lending to individuals for home purchase, where about 85% of the sector’s emissions occur.
- Specifies emissions scope: Scopes 1 and 2 dominate residential real estate emissions; Scope 3 is very limited.
- Chooses metric: physical intensity (kgCO2e/m2), which incentivizes more efficient assets and enables comparison across different asset sizes.
- Aligns pathway: uses the CRREM 1.5°C pathway for Spain and Portugal (EU real estate–specific) as the reference trajectory.
- Presents metric trend: shows a relatively flat trajectory around 23.6–23.7 kgCO2e/m2 in 2022–2023 with a planned decline to 19 kgCO2e/m2 by 2030.

nodes.title: Evolution of the metric
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.7.2 Evolution of the metric
nodes.start_phrase: The residential real estate metric remains practically stable since the baseline year.
nodes.summary:
- 2030 target: Reduce residential real estate financed emissions intensity by 19% from a 2022 baseline of 23.57 kgCO2e/m2 to 19.03 kgCO2e/m2. The metric has remained largely stable since the baseline, with reductions highly dependent on the energy mix.
- Value chain focus: Mortgage lending to individuals for home purchases, where ~85% of sector emissions are concentrated.
- Emissions scope: Primarily scopes 1 and 2 (direct combustion in housing and purchased energy); scope 3 is very limited.
- Metric: Physical intensity (kgCO2e/m2), chosen to incentivize exposure to more efficient assets and enable comparison across asset sizes.
- Reference pathway: CRREM 1.5°C trajectory for Spain and Portugal, aligned with the EU real estate sector.
- Sector transition plan with customers: Decarbonize through retrofitting existing dwellings and constructing higher-efficiency new buildings; increase availability of Energy Performance Certificates (EPCs) and building emissions data.
- Implementation constraints and enablers: Due to social sensitivity in this sector, CaixaBank’s direct ability to reduce intensity is limited; it will leverage governmental regulations and initiatives and contribute to the broader net‑zero transition.
- Current trajectory: CaixaBank’s metric is ~23.6–23.7 kgCO2e/m2 in 2022–2023, targeting 19 by 2030; CRREM pathway shows a steeper decline (indicative values ~14.1 to ~6.1).

nodes.title: Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.7.3 Sector transition plan – Actions with customers
nodes.start_phrase: In a similar way as in the commercial real estate sector, the decarbonisation of the residential real estate sector will be carried out by restoring the existing stock of dwellings and by constructing new building with higher energy efficiency ratings.
nodes.summary:
- CaixaBank sets a 2030 target to cut the residential real estate financed emissions intensity by 19% versus 2022.
- Baseline intensity: 23.57 kgCO2e/m2 (2022); targeted “arrival level” by 2030: 19.03 kgCO2e/m2.
- Metric has remained broadly stable since the baseline; progress is highly dependent on changes in the energy mix.
- Sector transition plan focuses on:
  - Retrofitting existing dwellings.
  - Constructing new homes with higher energy efficiency ratings.
  - Expanding availability of Energy Performance Certificates (EPCs) and emissions data for buildings.
  - Leveraging government regulations and initiatives due to CaixaBank’s limited direct ability to reduce customer emissions in this socially sensitive sector.
- Value chain focus: mortgage lending to individuals for home purchases, where ~85% of the residential real estate value chain’s emissions occur in the use phase.
- Emissions scope coverage: primarily scopes 1 (on-site combustion, e.g., heating) and 2 (purchased energy); scope 3 is very limited.
- Chosen metric: physical emissions intensity (kgCO2e/m2), which incentivizes more efficient assets and allows cross-asset comparability.
- Reference pathway: CRREM 1.5°C trajectory for Spain and Portugal, aligned with EU real estate sector guidance.
- Key design decisions documented: value chain definition, emissions scopes, intensity metric selection, and pathway choice.
- Reported trend: metric around 23.6 kgCO2e/m2 in 2022 and roughly stable in 2023 (about +0.4%), with a glidepath toward 19 kgCO2e/m2 by 2030.

nodes.title: Maritime sector
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.8 Maritime sector
nodes.start_phrase: The target for this sector has been calculated in line with the methodology of the Poseidon Principles, to which CaixaBank adhered in 2022.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Maritime sector decarbonisation target design and alignment metric for CaixaBank’s shipping portfolio.
- Framework: Targets set under the Poseidon Principles methodology, which CaixaBank joined in 2022.
- Metric: Alignment Delta (AD%)—a physical intensity metric measuring how a ship/portfolio’s carbon intensity deviates from the decarbonisation trajectory consistent with IMO targets.
- Baseline and target: 2022 baseline AD% = +11.9% (NZBA AD% from Poseidon for cargo ships). 2030 goal is AD% = 0%, implying a –11.9 percentage point improvement to reach alignment.
- Scope and boundary:
  - Value chain segment: Owner/Operator (port-to-port cargo transfer), as “use” phase accounts for ~92% of value-chain emissions.
  - Emissions scope: Scope 1 (fuel combustion during shipping), aligned with Poseidon coverage.
  - Asset coverage: Cargo ships only; passenger vessels (fast ferries, cruise ships) are currently excluded due to methodological inconsistencies in global alignment paths.
- Pathway: IMO’s initial 2018 scenario (2°C-consistent; 50% emissions reduction by 2050 vs. 2008) used as reference; pathway is being updated within Poseidon Principles.
- Governance: Target design will be further refined as Poseidon Principles update methodologies.

nodes.title: CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.heading: 1.6.3.4.8.1 CaixaBank's target by 2030
nodes.start_phrase: A reduction target for the AD% by 2030 intensity is established at 11.9%, with the following characteristics:
nodes.summary:
- Focus: CaixaBank’s maritime sector decarbonization approach, target design, and measurement framework.
- Methodology: Uses the Poseidon Principles (adopted by CaixaBank in 2022) to calculate portfolio alignment.
- Metric: Alignment Delta (AD%) based on physical emissions intensity; measures how a ship/portfolio aligns with decarbonization trajectories.
- Scope of emissions: Scope 1 fuel combustion during shipping (most material for the sector).
- Value chain boundary: Owner/Operator (port-to-port cargo transfer), as the use phase accounts for ~92% of value-chain emissions.
- Reference pathway: IMO’s 2018 initial strategy (2°C-consistent; 50% emissions reduction by 2050 vs 2008), with updates pending under Poseidon.
- Coverage: Cargo ships only; passenger vessels (fast ferries, cruise ships) excluded due to methodological inconsistencies in current alignment paths.
- Baseline and targets:
  - 2022 baseline AD%: 11.9% (Poseidon Principles cargo benchmark; NZBA reference).

- Objectives: Understand and manage climate impact and transition risks; inform decarbonization pathways to achieve net zero by 2050 in line with the NZBA commitment.
- Methodology: Based on the PCAF “Global GHG Accounting & Reporting Standard for the Financial Industry”; CaixaBank has been a PCAF member since 2021.
- Organizational scope: CaixaBank Group entities included are CaixaBank, CPC, and Bank BPI.
- Loan portfolio coverage (as of 31 Dec 2024): Mortgages, commercial real estate (CRE), corporate loans, project finance, and vehicle financing. For CPC, due to its business nature, only corporate loans, vehicle financing, and sovereign debt are included.
- Investment portfolio coverage: Emissions calculated for corporate bonds, sovereign debt, and equities with near-100% coverage. In 2024, sovereign debt-related emissions (as defined by PCAF, covering supranational loans and bonds and excluding sovereign bonds and loans) were estimated for the first time; results cover CaixaBank and CPC (not BPI).
- Data coverage: 86% of exposure within the calculation perimeter was computed; 14% was not calculated due to insufficient data.

nodes.title: Calculation method
nodes.heading: 1.6.4.1 Calculation method
nodes.start_phrase: The calculation has been performed under a bottom-up approach following the methodology developed by PCAF and described in "The Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard for the Financial Industry (Part A) Second Edition":
nodes.summary:
- Scope and approach: Bottom-up calculation of financed emissions using PCAF’s Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard (Part A, Second Edition), applying PCAF attribution factors and best available data for each asset class.
- Asset-class methodologies:
  - Mortgages and CRE: Emissions derived from property energy efficiency certificates; 2024 saw a major increase in actual certificates, improving data quality.
  - Business funding, equity, and corporate fixed income (non-sovereign): Based on financed companies’ reported Scope 1, 2, and 3 footprints; PCAF emission factors used when company data are unavailable.
  - Auto loans: Estimated by vehicle type and average mileage; improved in 2024 by incorporating fuel-type information when available.
  - Sovereign debt: Scope 1 financed emissions calculated on a production basis with and without LULUCF effects.
- Data systems: An internal tool integrates internal/external data to calculate, monitor, and track financed emissions, supporting quality, completeness, and carbon-neutrality management.
- Portfolio results and trends:
  - 2024 total financed emissions: 78,243 ktCO2e (Scope 1+2: 24,448; Scope 3: 53,795) on calculated exposure of €277,546 M (out of €321,123 M perimeter). 2023 total: 84,588 ktCO2e on €275,803 M, reflecting a ~7.5% reduction.
  - Key drivers of the reduction: Improved data quality (more actual company/project data) and a continuing decline in Scope 1+2 emissions of financed companies since 2021. In 2024, actual data for three significant projects in the coal sector reduced estimated Scope 1+2 by ~9,000 ktCO2e versus PCAF factor-based estimates.
  - Expected variability: Financed emissions may fluctuate over time due to company valuation changes, data availability, calculation process improvements, and updates to PCAF factors.
- 2024 breakdown highlights:
  - By asset class (calculated exposure share in parentheses): Business funding (74.2%) dominates emissions (S1+2: 19,553 kt; S3: 53,528 kt; intensity 162 tCO2e/€M). Mortgages (99.9%) S1+2: 2,825 kt (23 t/€M). Auto loans (95.2%) S1+2: 1,891 kt (211 t/€M). CRE (88.0%) S1+2: 72 kt (13 t/€M). Corporate fixed income (99.0%) S1+2: 108 kt; S3: 266 kt (6 t/€M). Equity immaterial.
  - By sector (business funding): Largest S1+2 totals in oil & gas (3,539 kt), transport (3,083 kt), agriculture (2,421 kt), and electric utilities (1,598 kt). High intensities in cement (1,443 t/€M), iron & steel (281 t/€M), aluminium (195 t/€M), and coal (very high intensity on small exposure).
  - By geography: Exposure concentrated in Spain/Portugal (S1+2: 20,168 kt; intensity 81 t/€M), with Europe at 88 t/€M and Rest of world at 355 t/€M.
- Sovereign debt (2024): €50,082 M exposure; Scope 1 emissions 7,174 ktCO2e (with LULUCF) or 8,195 ktCO2e (without); intensities 143 and 164 tCO2e/€M, respectively. BPI sovereign holdings excluded.
- 2023 comparatives: Higher total S1+2 (33,840 kt) and intensity (122 t/€M) with notable factor-driven spikes in certain NACE codes (e.g., coal), illustrating sensitivity to PCAF factor updates.
- Notes: Results include CO2e across CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6, NF3; minor rounding differences may occur.

nodes.title: Calculation considerations
nodes.heading: 1.6.4.2 Calculation considerations
nodes.start_phrase: The latest financial and emissions information available for the companies in the CaixaBank, CPC and BPI2 portfolios was used in the calculation.
nodes.summary:
- Sets out Annex 1 methodology for calculating financed emissions for CaixaBank, CPC and BPI portfolios in the 2024 Management Report.
- Data sources and hierarchy:
  - Uses the latest available company financials and emissions data.
  - Where company data are missing, applies PCAF sectoral GHG intensity factors (tCO2e/€m turnover) from the September 2024 publication (dated March 2024).
  - For real estate, uses EPC ratings and emission intensity by property type/geography from Spain’s IDAE and CRREM (factors as published by PCAF in March 2024, dated September 2023).
  - When portfolio companies’ reporting periods differ, the most recent annual data are used.
- Boundary and approach:
  - Operational control approach following PCAF methodology.
- Asset classes covered and valuation basis:
  - Corporate finance (non-financial corporates): loans for general corporate purposes (including SMEs) and project finance.
  - Corporate financing and fixed income: company value equals book-value equity plus book-value debt for both listed and unlisted firms.
  - Mortgages and commercial real estate: emissions estimated using EPCs and location/property-type intensity benchmarks.
  - Sovereign debt: PCAF production approach, attributing emissions to domestic production (domestic consumption plus exports) per UNFCCC inventories.
- Scope treatment and reporting:
  - Scope 3 calculated across all sectors in the portfolio.
  - Due to high double-counting risk in Scope 3, disclosure is limited to emissions intensity per €m for Scopes 1+2.
- Exclusions and limitations:
  - Assets with insufficient data excluded; exposures to credit institutions are outside the perimeter.
  - Anomalous PCAF factor for NACE 35.20 corrected via a conservative approach: apply the highest emission factor within the “Electricity, gas & water” sector by geography.
- Assurance:
  - 2024 financed emissions footprint subject to limited assurance by PwC in accordance with ISAE 3410 (NIEA 3410).

  - Category 15 “Investments” (financed emissions) represents ~99% of Scope 3 and is addressed separately (“Calculation of financed CO2 emissions”).
  - Excluding category 15, a 2022 materiality analysis identified categories 3.1 Purchased goods and services, 3.2 Capital goods, 3.3 Fuel and energy-related activities, and 3.6 Corporate travel as material for operational management.
- Explains boundary setting:
  - The 2022 analysis (covering 16 Group companies, 98% of assets) defined a new perimeter for the operational carbon footprint including only material categories.
  - Progress against 2022–2024 reduction targets is assessed using the pre-2022 (old) perimeter on which those targets were set.
  - The Environmental Management perimeter covers 99.4% of employees.
- Confirms governance and updates:
  - A 2024 internal review validated the continued relevance of the 2022 materiality conclusions.
  - A new materiality study will be conducted in 2025 using 2024 data.
- States the methodological basis: GHG Protocol standards (WRI/WBCSD) for Scopes 1–3, with Scope 3 aligned to the Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard.

nodes.title: Scope 1 and 2
nodes.heading: 1.6.5.1.1.1.1 Scope 1 and 2
nodes.start_phrase: The emission factors used to calculate the footprint of scopes 1 and 2 have been obtained from the Carbon footprint, offsetting and absorption projects registry of June 2024 for Spain.
nodes.summary:
- Defines the methodology for calculating Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions.
- Emission factors: Spain uses the June 2024 Carbon footprint, offsetting and absorption projects registry; Portugal and Luxembourg use IPCC Fifth Assessment Report GWP values.
- Scope 1 coverage: facility fuels (Gas Oil C, propane, natural gas), vehicle fleet fuel, and cooling/refrigerant gases.
- Scope 1 data quality: primarily actual data; exceptions include:
  - Gas Oil C for territorial branches estimated from purchased amounts and the average fuel price published by IDEA.
  - Vehicle fuel use estimated from odometer readings and theoretical consumption by vehicle model.
- Scope 2 accounting: market-based approach with 0 emissions when backed by 100% renewable certificates or suppliers with a 100% renewable mix.
- Energy consumption reporting in kWh; mostly sourced from invoices, with remaining data estimated via software using monthly average consumption and pro‑rata values per supply point over the past three years.
- Extract from the Management Report 2024 (p. 299).

nodes.title: Scope 3
nodes.heading: 1.6.5.1.1.1.2 Scope 3
nodes.start_phrase: The methodology presented below in relation to the calculation of material categories of scope 3 according to the materiality analysis of scope 3 categories (ä see section “Materiality analysis of Scope 3 categories ”), except for category 3.15, which is presented in section ä “Calculation of financed C O2 emissions ”.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Methodology and results for Scope 3 emissions, aligned with a materiality analysis of categories; category 3.15 (Investments) is treated separately in a dedicated section.
- Categories 3.1 (Purchased goods and services) and 3.2 (Capital goods): 2024 method uses 100% of operating expenses and investments as the base, excluding emissions already counted in other scopes and non-emitting spend (e.g., taxes, fees).
- Data sources and factors: Supplier invoices are multiplied by supplier-specific emission intensities (supplier carbon footprint/turnover) gathered via CaixaBank’s carbon footprint survey (to suppliers with turnover > €0.5M) and public disclosures; if unavailable, sector emission factors from PCAF are used.
- 2024 methodology enhancements:
  - Coverage expanded to 100% of suppliers (vs. 80% previously).
  - PCAF intensities adopted as the conversion fallback.
  - Updated supplier questionnaire to obtain specific emission factors.
  - In 2024, 15% (3.1) and 24% (3.2) of emissions were calculated using supplier-specific factors; the 2025–2027 Environmental Management Plan targets increasing these shares via supplier engagement.
- Backcasted results: 2021–2023 Scope 3.1 and 3.2 emissions recalculated with the new method, applying filters to remove double counting and non-emitting spend, prioritizing supplier data and complemented by PCAF:
  - 3.1 (tCO2e): 2023: 158,001 → 229,493; 2022: 128,006 → 237,891; 2021: 146,724 → 235,307.
  - 3.2 (tCO2e): 2023: 46,756 → 90,016; 2022: 60,811 → 100,634; 2021: 45,842 → 101,065.
- Category 3.3 (Fuels and energy-related activities): Includes well-to-tank (WTT) and transmission & distribution (T&D) losses; Scope 1 fuels multiplied by DEFRA WTT factors; Scope 2 electricity multiplied by IEA factors for WTT and T&D.
- Category 3.6 (Business travel): Calculated with DEFRA factors using actual mileage by mode (air, rail, rental, company cars) and hotel nights; no estimates used due to complete actual data.
- 2024 environmental performance snapshot vs. 2023:
  - Scope 1 gross emissions: 7.28 ktCO2e (−13.55%).
  - Scope 2 gross emissions (location-based): 23.05 ktCO2e (−21.57%); market-based: 0.
  - Scope 3 total gross emissions: 82,164.57 ktCO2e (−7.32%), with category 15 (Investments) dominating and decreasing to 81,838.05 ktCO2e (−7.33%). Reported 2024 values include: 3.1 Purchased goods and services 229.49 kt; 3.2 Capital goods 72.70 kt; 3.3 Fuels and energy-related activities 5.12 kt; 3.6 Corporate travel 12.45 kt.
- Governance and targets context:
  - 2024 reduction targets were set using a previous carbon footprint perimeter.
  - Scope 3.6 historical data adjusted due to reclassification of certain flights from medium- to short-haul (<1,000 km).
  - Decarbonization targets published under NZBA (lending sectors) and NZAOA (insurance corporate portfolio); sovereign debt excluded; baseline years detailed elsewhere.
  - Notes: Some operational data involve estimates if unavailable at reporting close; for value-chain entities with different reporting periods, the latest available annual data are used.

nodes.heading: 1.6.5.1.2 Breakdown of operational emissions from scope 1, 2, and 3 by gas type for 2024 (T CO2 eq)

nodes.summary:
